name: r4-m09
statement: Olmo-3.1-RL-Zero-Code's math gain over the cued base is a transferred ending policy (finish under the cap with one terminal answer, then stop), learned because 3.1 scores truncated rollouts as failures; on problems the base finishes cleanly but wrongly, Code behaves like a fresh base sample and adds no correctness.
scope: Covers allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code (1ca3bb30) vs allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token opening cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, on MATH-500 and the clean hard328; also explains why Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Code (3.0, truncations masked) gives no math gain. Does not cover the Math-RL gain (which may add real correctness), T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 settings where the base loops, code benchmarks, or other model families.

imports.finding: Masking the reward of truncated responses helps at an 8k cap but at long caps (20k) leaves models writing longer, repetitive, non-terminating outputs that are clipped more often.
imports.how: Explains the split between the two Code releases: 3.0 masked truncations at a long cap and so never learned to terminate (its rollouts loop on code), while 3.1 trained truncations as negatives and learned a cap-avoiding, single-final-answer ending that transfers to math.

explains.quote: Code 3.1 cue 450 is +7.8 pts [4.4, 11.2] over Code 3.0 cue
explains.how: Only 3.1 penalised truncation, so only 3.1 carries the ending policy, regardless of which moved the weights further.

explains.quote: not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: This is the recipe difference that teaches the ending policy in 3.1 and not in 3.0.
The plain base fails mostly at the ending (missing or unparsable answer line, cap hits), which an ending policy repairs without any math skill.
Code answers are shorter than the base's 3,933 tokens, as expected from a policy that commits and stops before the cap.
On hard328 the base loses 77 problems to the cap; Code's lower token count reflects finishing those, which is where its gain comes from.

explains.quote: 8 right answer in a rejected or garbled final line
explains.how: Part of the base's errors are ending failures with correct math, which a clean terminal answer fixes.

explains.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
explains.how: Recovery travels with the ending format, consistent with a format and termination component carrying much of the gain.

conflicts.how: Code 3.0 writes even shorter answers (3,069 tokens/problem) and should rarely hit the cap, yet gains nothing; finishing early is not enough by itself, so the theory has to rest on the clean single-terminal-answer part, which no item measures for 3.0.
Code matches half the Math delta on hard328, which a shared correctness component would also predict; the theory must claim the match is a coincidence of ending repairs versus real fixes.

rival: Code 3.1 shares a domain-general deliberate-and-verify component with Math RL (m03 and r3 theories), so it fixes clean finished-but-wrong base answers as well as ending failures. What separates the two is Code's fix rate on base problems that finished without a cap hit but were wrong. This theory says it equals a fresh base sample's (random cell on MATH-500, about 0.15 on hard328). The rival says it is near RL's (RL fixes 33 of the 90 hard328 finished-wrong problems, 0.37).

predictions.experiment: MATH-500: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base hit the cap and was wrong
predictions.recipe: Read studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; select problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == true. Statistic: number of selected problems with score_v3 == 1 in 0203, divided by the number of selected problems.

predictions.experiment: Generate 4 samples per problem from Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code (1ca3bb30, RL tokenizer) with the cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, no restarts, seeds 74,000,000 + 10,000*sample + problem_index, on the MATH-500 problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == false in per_problem.json (about 63 problems, about 250 generations, one H100). Grade with v3. Compare per-sample accuracy to the cued base's 4 samples on the same problems from studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0 rows only).
predictions.unit: percentage points (Code minus base per-sample accuracy over problem-sample pairs)
predictions.refuted_by: Code's per-sample accuracy exceeds the base's by more than 10 points on these problems, or Code hits the cap in more than 3 % of its generations
